summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: Bertha's Visit to Her Uncle in England (Mrs. Marcet, 3 vols, 1830)

**Frame:** Journal of Bertha Montague (b. ~1808, Rio de Janeiro), daughter of late Colonel Montague and of Brazilian-resident widow (mother, unable to travel; her "Mamma," who was a loving but ill-judging parent; sister Marianne left behind). Sailed on H.M.S. Phaeton (Captain M.) with Mrs. P----, arrived Falmouth 31 June-ish 1829 (Vol 1 journal). Uncle = Mr. Montague's brother-in-law? No: uncle is Mamma's brother, a Mr. Montague (called "my uncle"; name not given beyond uncle). Lives at **Fernhurst**, on the border of the **Forest of Deane**, Gloucestershire, near the Severn. Aunt (mother of cousins). Cousins: **Mary** (timid, delicate, clear-headed, arithmetic teacher), **Caroline** (handsome, bright complexion, punctual, useful, mild temper), **Wentworth** and **Frederick** (boys; Frederick is Caroline's "little boy" charge; Frederick collects insects, fond of questions), **Grace** (little sister, play-fellow of uncle). Uncle's name rarely used. Lumley family (Mr. Fitzroy Lumley, formerly Mr. Carl? no: Mr. Lumley = Fitzroy, formerly "Fitzroy" of Strath-morton; wife Mrs. Lumley; two daughters, Miss Lumleys). Mr. Benson, good clergyman. Mr. Biggs (gardening friend), Lord S----.

**Key characters in Vol 1:**
- Farmer Moreland & Dame Moreland (harvest home, Christmas visits).
- Blind basket-maker (old man, wife dead/sick; foster daughter **Bessy Grimley**, b. ~21; engaged to **James Franklin**, emigrated to America, returned; married; farm near Fernhurst).
- Mrs. P---- (Mrs. P, Gertrude? later revealed as Gertrude; rescued in Jamaica).
- Mr. H----, Mr. Maude family (Miss Maudes, Elmore), Mrs. Ando (Newnham), Madeleine & Bertram (Swiss/Savoyard; Bertram English officer, father clergyman in Wales).
- Colonel Travers (Ceylon/India; Vol 1-2 storyteller).
- Gypsy boy "Charley" (Quick-finger), mother a dying gipsy woman, found by Wentworth & Frederick.
- Mr. Lumley's story: formerly Fitzroy, married Mrs. Lumley (sad hymn author).

**Mrs. P's narrative (Vol 2 "Mrs. P.'s Narrative"):** Gertrude; wife of Edward P. (college friend of brother); lived at Ulleswater; extravagance & debt; Mr. Crispin (old friend, Jamaica estate San Pedro); Nanina (Jamaican servant girl, falsely accused of theft of ring found in book); Apakong (Maroon-descendant rebel); insurrection; hurricane wrecked ship off Hayti; Mrs. P recovered; Nanina freed; Phaëton to Brazil. Mrs. P's rules: "Buy nothing you don't absolutely want...Waste nothing... ORDER..."

**Vol 1 episodes (selected, in order):** Atlantic voyage (phaeton bird, petrels, flying fish, Gulf Stream, sea-weed, salt test with towel, falls of albatross, Azores, Cornwall, Falmouth 31 June); arrival Fernhurst Aug 3; Sabbath lecture (Sumner); breakfast rules; Bessy & Franklin; Staffa/Hertford letters (Hertford = cousin visiting Western Isles: Staffa, Skye, North Rona, Lewis, St Kilda, Islay); glowworm; forest of Dean; Farmer Moreland's harvest home; Bessy story; Lumleys at Fernhurst; Mrs. Lumley's hymn; Auvergne; mirage; Joseph/Pharaoh/Moses lessons; Babylon; Kelek; Stockholm; potatoes; Canova; Tempest; Milner's? (no). Vol 1 ends with locust swarm arithmetic (Colonel Travers, Smyrna 1811; 168,608,563,200,000 locusts).

**Vol 2 key events:** Pepper; Davy horse-shoe musician; Passover; Rice/paddy; Ceylon Bedah story (Ceylonese man, pearl, banyan, dog); Tempest; Mozart; Ten Commandments; Christmas (mummers, Yule); Psalm 45; Farmer Moreland's Christmas visit; **Charley the gipsy boy** (mother dies); Scouler voyage (Juan Fernandez); Chinese fish/ants; Hebrew Sabbath/Moses; Mrs. P's narrative (Ulleswater, Jamaica, Nanina, rebellion, Haiti shipwreck); dormouse (torpor); toads in plaster; snails; prophecies; frost (sallows); hyacinths; Canada letters (Cobourg, Loghouse); Herculaneum; Vol 2 ends Apr-May, ants & aphids.

**Vol 3:** Hebrew festivals; Balaam; Moses' death; Penrhyn slate quarries; Bangor; Holyhead; Llangollen aqueduct. Bertha's final letter from **Holyhead**, 23 June 1830 (end of journal).

## BOOK 2: The Slave of Silence (F. M. White, 1904)

**Setting:** London. Beatrice Darryll (22, ash-blonde, blue eyes, "Slave of Silence"). Father **Sir Charles Darryll** (charming, reckless, City speculator; faces prosecution over City company; shares guaranteed by daughter's marriage). Wedding to **Stephen Richford** (millionaire, thick lip, heavy, shifty, drinks; crooked City man) set for 12 noon at church, reception in **Royal Palace Hotel**. Beatrice's former lover: **Mark Ventmore** (painter, son of wealthy City father; disowned for art; in Paris/Venice). Mark's father is a shrewd, grey-eyed City man (cheque-book; later pays off debts). **Colonel Berrington** (brilliant soldier, long leave, Egypt campaign, Madi Halfa; love of Mary Grey, Mary's brother's sister). **Mary Sartoris (later Mary Grey)**, grey lady, "Slave of Silence"/"Slave of the Bond"; ex-fiancée of Berrington; brother **Carl Sartoris** (alias Carl Grey; ex-fiancé of Violet Decie; crippled after Simla affair; invalid chair; arch-criminal; electric torture devices; chair "Tiger"-like).

**Other characters:** Lady Rashborough (Adela) and Lord Rashborough (gave bride away). Adeline (maid). Dr. Andrews; Dr. Oswin (family doctor). Inspector Field (Scotland Yard). Catton and Benwort (hall porter, night watchman). Countess de la Moray and General Gastang (alias "Cora" and "Reggie"; real names). Dr. James Bentwood (ex-army surgeon, Eastern drugs; hulking, red face). The "Rajah of Ahbad" (Eastern-dressed renegade; Rajah's suite, salt bullet). Violet Decie = actress "Adela Vane" (Comedy Theatre). Lady Parkstone (her aunt). Mr. George Fleming (lawyer, Lincoln's Inn Fields). Acton (law stationer, forgery). Macklin (police constable). Sartoris's neighbour house No. 14 Audley Place.

**Plot events, in order:**
1. Night before wedding, Royal Palace Hotel. Sir Charles threatens Beatrice; men watch him; City company fraud; bank cheque; Beatrice wrote to Mark (letter undelivered).
2. Dinner. Colonel Berrington seated by Beatrice. Grey lady ("Slave of the Bond") appears; Berrington's search for her. Swiss waiter gives Beatrice wine card: pencilled note in Mark's handwriting. Mark disguised as waiter, meets Beatrice in conservatory; she refuses to elope (father's honour).
3. Wedding morning: Richford gives diamonds (Rockmartin gems, £40,000). Beatrice refuses kiss. Ceremony interrupted by Mark: Sir Charles found dead in bed, body hours cold. Beatrice flees with Mark.
4. Beatrice finds telegram from Richford (grey paper, time ~10 a.m.) by father's body. Richford confronted; she refuses to live with him. Richford strikes Mark; Mark floors him.
5. Luncheon: salt bullet on Richford's steak (Richford drinks heavily, flees to Sartoris at 100 Audley Place).
6. Beatrice to Lady Rashborough (rejected). Jeweller's in Bond Street (cash £200+). Countess (Cora) and General (Reggie) befriend Beatrice; Countess claims to know father. Countess takes wax impression of seals; drugs Beatrice with perfume.
7. Morning: body missing from sealed suite. Night watchman Catton and porter Benwort attacked, bound; blood on carpet, button "R.P.H." Rajah's suite holds them.
8. Berrington and Field stake out 100 Audley Place (Wandsworth Common). Secret room, dining-room table lift; Richford present; Sartoris gives orders; Mary talks with Berrington.
9. Berrington imprisoned; Sartoris tortures; Burmese rubies (Burmese visitors); Berrington escapes; signal lights; Berrington shot two Burmese.
10. Mary delivers Berrington's forged letter to Beatrice (letter at Royal Palace). Beatrice goes to Audley Place (hansom; Carl's laughter); Richford tries to get diamonds; Countess/Reggie take diamonds; Beatrice escapes; Berrington rescues her.
11. Field gets Sir Charles' deed (forgery: stamp dated 4 April 1893; Acton forged). Sir Charles's collar found in vault under dining-room.
12. Final arrests at 100 Audley Place; Richford killed in motor-car crash on bridge; Sartoris dies of punctured lung; Bentwood arrested.
13. Sir Charles alive (drugged, hidden at Wandsworth by Sartoris); Mark's father buys concessions; Sir Charles goes to country with Beatrice; Berrington marries Mary Grey; Mark and Beatrice marry later.

**Concluding lines:** "Thank God no longer the Slave of Silence!" (Mary).

---

**Notes for two-book answers:** Two separate books; keep names/events within each. Book 1 is epistolary-style journal in multiple letters with dates; Book 2 is a novel with chapters I–XL.
